summary: Washington/Tillamook county line lookout: 1932 crow's nest, Tom Stevenson in 1930s, destroyed by 1933 fire, 40-ft tower 1947-1974; no current site description.

facts.design: Originally a 90-foot crow's nest with enclosed platform and shake cabin (1932); later a 40-foot pole L-4 tower (FFLOS) or 40-foot timber tower with 14x14 cab (weebly)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1974 per FFLOS, firelookout.com and weebly; the 1933 fire destroyed the earlier lookout

events.note: Tom Stevenson in a lookout 90 feet above the ground; a cougar killed his dog at the foot of the tree (1930 event described in 1931 item)
FFLOS dates the 90-foot crow's nest to 1932; a Tillamook district report records a log lookout house built that year; newspaper items show a lookout by 1930
Wilson River fire drove Stevenson from his post in August 1933; an August 26 report says the lookout was destroyed by fire. The FFLOS register does not mention this
Activated March 10, 1942 and deactivated October 19, 1942 under the Portland Filter Center; a July 1942 memo recommended dropping it as an observation post
FFLOS and firelookout.com: 40-foot pole L-4 tower replaced the crow's nest in 1947; weebly dates a tower to 1946 and a 40-foot timber tower completed in 1948
Removed in 1974 per all three sources
Registered November 15, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: The record's 5.5 m (about 18 ft) matches only the 1944 18-foot tower in the weebly history. The lookout standing until 1974 was a 40-foot tower per FFLOS and the weebly 1948 entry.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says a 90-foot crow's nest was erected in 1932 and the weebly history quotes a 1932 log lookout house. Newspaper items from 1930 and 1931 already describe a lookout tower on the mountain (the 1931 item puts Stevenson 90 feet up), so the register's 1932 date may not be the first structure. The story uses the register date and states the newspaper evidence.

FFLOS and firelookout.com date the 40-foot pole L-4 tower to 1947; the weebly history dates a tower to 1946 (cost for the tower only) and a 40-foot timber tower with a 14x14 cab to 1948. The removal date of 1974 agrees across all three.
FFLOS gives 3,460 ft (1,055 m); firelookout.com gives 3464 ft. The brief's 1054.6 m is consistent with the FFLOS figure.

The FFLOS record does not mention the 1933 fire. The weebly newspaper items conflict: one from August 25 says it is unknown whether the lookout or the cabin burned; the August 26 item says the lookout was destroyed by fire. The story reports both: the August 25 item says the lookout or cabin burning was still unknown, and the August 26 report says the lookout was destroyed.

notes_for_editor: The brief's note that the record shares a register number is not borne out: this record is FFLOS US 733 (OR 142). A separate FFLOS page for Saddle Mountain (US 734, OR 143) describes a different site with a 1922 platform removed in 1953; it was not merged here. Almost all history detail comes from one site, the Rex's Fire Lookout Page, quoting newspapers and agency reports; the FFLOS and firelookout.com entries give only the construction, rebuild and removal dates. No source describes the site since 1974; the 1941 survey note is the most recent description of remains. Access was not covered by any source read, so the access facts are omitted.
